basis: PHYH-related Refsum disease: retinal degeneration nearly universal; neuropathy and hearing loss in most. Ichthyosis omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Disease located in the mitral valve; an immune mechanism does not apply across the umbrella.
Defined by impaired visual function; neurologic causes occur in subsets and do not justify a second axis across the umbrella.
Inherited keratoconus causes corneal thinning and ectasia.
Follicular keratosis with scarring and hair loss. Absent eyelashes are hair involvement; epiphora alone does not establish ocular damage.
An infantile interstitial lung disease involving pulmonary neuroendocrine cells; not an endocrine gland disorder.
Otosclerosis affects the otic capsule and hearing apparatus; localized ear bone remodeling does not warrant a musculoskeletal axis.
Congenital loss of nociception and smell reflects sensory neuronal dysfunction. Fractures and neuropathic arthropathy result from unrecognized injury.
Heterogeneous 11p deletion umbrella; neurodevelopmental impairment is common across major deletion syndromes. Eye, skeletal and renal findings depend on the deleted region.
Contractures and impaired proprioception define the disease; scoliosis 10/10 and areflexia 9/9. Respiratory insufficiency reported in 6/6; reflux only 2/11.
Defined clinical spectrum includes retinal degeneration with early deafness and respiratory ciliary dysfunction; expression varies by variant.
Benign vascular lesion arising in the retina; no evidence of common systemic vascular disease.
Cerebral motor injury produces spasticity of all four limbs. Altered muscle tone alone does not establish primary muscle damage.
Congenital dysferlin-related skeletal myopathy with weakness and hypotonia; delayed motor milestones reflect muscle dysfunction.
Immunodeficiency with anemia 3/3 and leukopenia 2/3; cholangitis 3/3 and conductive hearing loss 2/2. Cutaneous warts and duodenitis omitted by cap.
Defined as disease affecting the brain, spinal cord or peripheral nerves; subtype-specific organs are not generalized.
Chronic loss of liver function. Hepatic encephalopathy and hepatorenal syndrome are separately diagnosed complications.
Congenital atrial septal defect; additional reported abnormalities also involve cardiac structures or conduction.
Autoimmune orbital inflammation in a euthyroid patient; thyroid dysfunction is not required and subsequent thyroid disease is a separate diagnosis.
Skeletal dysplasia and amelogenesis imperfecta define the syndrome. Hearing impairment occurs in 4/4 annotated patients.
Bone fragility, joint hypermobility and hyperextensible fragile skin define this overlap syndrome. Blue sclerae are non-damaging; arterial rupture only 1/5.
Persistent fetal ocular vasculature with severe vitreoretinal maldevelopment and blindness; no systemic vascular involvement established.
Autoimmune inflammatory disease of oral mucosa. Extraoral cutaneous lichen planus is not required for this oral concept.
Intellectual disability and progressive skeletal abnormalities define syndrome. Hypodontia/dental defects 80–99%; hearing loss reported 1/1, with limited frequency evidence.
Muscle tissue disease under the musculoskeletal umbrella. Cardiac and other specialized muscle disorders are subsets, not shared additional involvement.
